To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the MESH approach can help improve health systems; (2) the MESH building process is not easy; (3) the MESH process is not linear; (4) the MESH model is not a one size fits all; (5) MESH is a long-term investment; and (6) the MESH concept is a useful way to help build health systems.

MESH is a useful approach to building capacity for health in disadvantaged communities; MESH is a way of building the capacity of communities to implement health services; MESH is not just about building health facilities; and MESH is not a one-off event but a process.

MESH is the most appropriate approach to strengthening public health systems in poor areas, and that MESH building strategies should be implemented at the local level in consultation with communities and other stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we can build MESH infrastructure that will help to achieve the MDGs.
how to build health systems in a more effective manner.
building capacity for health systems in poor areas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MESH is a very useful concept that needs to be further developed and tested in different contexts and settings.
the MESH approach is useful for the development and strengthening of health systems.
the MESH approach is a promising way forward for the MDGs and the health sector in particular.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MESH approach provides a useful tool to improve the capacity to deliver health services to the most disadvantaged communities in South Africa.
MESH is an important tool to help us to think more clearly about how we can improve the health of poor communities and to help us to build a more effective health system.
MESH can be a useful framework for building capacity in poor areas to improve their health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health system must be seen as part of a broader system that needs to be strengthened if the health system is to be effective.

MESH building is a critical component of the health system that is often neglected in the literature and that it can be a useful tool to improve the effectiveness of health programs in disadvantaged communities and districts.

there are no quick fixes and that there is a need to develop a more holistic approach that takes into account the complex interactions within the public health systems and between these systems and civil society.
